mainTopic: Whether a תם's חצי נזק is ממון or קנס, its practical results in בבל, and the new משנה on five תמין and five מועדין.
overview: There is a key rule: a person who admits on his own to something that carries a קנס does not pay, but if it is ממון, his own admission makes him pay. The גמרא tries twice to prove from a משנה in כתובות that the חצי נזק of a תם is ממון. The first proof, from 'my ox killed so-and-so's ox,' is pushed off: the whole משנה is about a מועד. The second proof, from the rule that only someone paying MORE than the damage is exempt on admission, ends in a תיובתא. Even so, the גמרא rules פלגא נזקא קנסא. It explains that the משנה could not make a blanket rule about paying less, because חצי נזק צרורות is ממון. The practical result: an unusual attack by a dog or cat is not collected in בבל, but the victim keeps what he seizes, can force a hearing in ארץ ישראל, and the owner is placed in נידוי until he removes the danger, based on רבי נתן. A new משנה then lists five תם acts and five מועד cases, including wild animals. The גמרא shows that the first part of that list follows the רבנן and the later part follows רבי טרפון, as שמואל taught. Finally, רבי אלעזר in the name of רב begins a different explanation, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The source: admitting your ox killed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: if someone admits his ox killed a person or another person's ox, he pays based on his own admission.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a person says, 'My ox killed so-and-so,' or 'My ox killed so-and-so's ox,' he pays because of what he himself said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a משנה (from כתובות) as raw material for a proof. This step sets up the next move, where the גמרא will try to read this source a certain way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are no witnesses here, only the owner's own confession. Normally, admitting to a קנס does not make you pay, but admitting to ממון does. So the fact that he pays tells us this payment counts as ממון.

keyTerms.meaning: pays based on his own admission (without witnesses)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think he pays because witnesses saw it. The whole point is that he pays only because of his own confession, and that is what makes this משנה useful for telling ממון apart from קנס.

phrases.english: "My ox killed so-and-so"
or "[my ox killed] so-and-so's ox"

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה מְשַׁלֵּם עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: this person pays based on his own admission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source into the larger question of whether חצי נזק is קנס or ממון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who admits his ox killed a person or another's ox pays based on his own admission.

steps.title: Suggesting the source is about a תם ox
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה is talking about a תם ox. That would prove חצי נזק is ממון, since it is paid based on one's own admission.
steps.simpleTranslation: What, isn't this talking about a תם ox?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes reading the משנה as being about a תם ox, in order to prove that the half-payment of a תם is ממון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תם ox that kills another ox pays only חצי נזק. If a person pays that half-damage just because he admitted it, it cannot be a קנס, because someone who admits to a קנס does not pay. So חצי נזק would be ממון.

keyTerms.meaning: what, is it not...? (a phrase that offers a reading to prove a point)
an ox that has not yet established a habit of goring; it pays half damage

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main attempt in this section to settle whether חצי נזק is ממון or קנס, which decides whether a confession makes a person pay.

phrases.english: What, is it not [talking] about an innocuous ox?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the quoted משנה as being about a תם, to draw a proof from it.
steps.raayaObject: That חצי נזק of a תם is ממון, not קנס.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in כתובות: one who admits his ox killed another's ox pays based on his own admission.

steps.title: No, it is about a מועד ox
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the משנה could be talking about a מועד ox, whose full payment is clearly ממון.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about a forewarned (מועד) ox.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof by saying the משנה might be about a מועד ox, not a תם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מועד pays full damage, and everyone agrees that is ממון. So paying on one's own admission there proves nothing about the half-payment of a תם.

keyTerms.meaning: a forewarned ox with an established habit of goring; it pays full damage

phrases.english: No, [it is talking] about a forewarned ox.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of step 2 by moving the משנה to a מועד case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not prove that חצי נזק is a קנס.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the משנה is about a תם, but it could just as easily be about a מועד.

steps.title: So would a תם not pay on admission?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the משנה is only about a מועד, does that mean a תם would not pay based on admission?
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about a תם? Would you say that indeed he does not pay based on his own admission?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out what the pushback in step 3 would mean for a תם. This step sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה had to be limited to a מועד, the reason would be that a תם is different, meaning it would not pay on admission. The גמרא makes the pushback admit this so it can test it.

phrases.english: But [with] an innocuous ox, what [would the law be]?

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי דְּאֵין מְשַׁלֵּם עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ?
phrases.english: Would you say that indeed he does not pay based on his own admission?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what the pushback in step 3 implies about a תם.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the pushback really means that a תם does not pay on its owner's admission.

steps.title: Then the משנה should have split the same case
steps.stepSummary: If a תם would not pay on admission, the משנה should have taught that within the same case ('this is only for a מועד, but a תם does not pay'). Instead it moved on to a new case about a slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, instead of teaching in the next clause, 'My ox killed so-and-so's slave, he does not pay based on his own admission,' the משנה should have made a split in the same case and taught: 'When is this said? With a מועד. But with a תם, he does not pay based on his own admission!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the pushback. If a תם were really exempt when the owner admits, the משנה would have shown the קנס/ממון difference using the תם/מועד split in the same case, not by bringing a new case of a slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The next clause of the משנה, about killing a slave, is there to show a case of קנס, where admitting does not make you pay. If a תם's half-damage were also a קנס, the easier way to teach this would be to split the first case itself. Since the משנה did not do that, it seems a תם does pay on admission, so חצי נזק is ממון.

keyTerms.meaning: the latter clause of a משנה
let it make a split and teach it within the same case
in what case is this said? (a phrase that limits a rule)

steps.whatToRemember: This challenge revives the proof: since the משנה did not split the case into מועד and תם, it seems a תם pays on its owner's admission. The next step answers it, so this does not end up proving that חצי נזק is ממון.
steps.confusionAlert: The slave case is not about damages to property. Killing a slave carries a fixed payment that is a קנס, and that is exactly why admitting to it does not make you pay.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic 'why didn't the משנה teach it the simpler way' argument. The גמרא learns the law from how the משנה chose to build its cases.

phrases.english: If so,
rather than teaching in the latter clause
"My ox killed so-and-so's slave"
he does not pay based on his own admission,
let it make a split and teach it within the same case:
phrases.notes: 'The same case' means the first case, an ox killing someone's ox.

phrases.english: In what case is this said? With a forewarned ox,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּתָם – אֵינוֹ מְשַׁלֵּם עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ!
phrases.english: but with an innocuous ox, he does not pay based on his own admission!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the pushback of step 3, using what it implies (from step 4) about a תם.
steps.kashyaTarget: The pushback that the משנה is talking only about a מועד ox.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a תם did not pay on admission, the משנה would have shown the קנס example by splitting the first case into מועד and תם, rather than bringing a separate case about a slave. Since it did not, a תם must pay on admission.

steps.title: The whole משנה is about a מועד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the קשיא of step 5: the משנה never mentions a תם at all, because every case in it is about a מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The entire משנה is talking about a מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 5. The משנה did not say 'but a תם does not pay' because the משנה is not discussing a תם anywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 asked why the משנה did not draw the line between תם and מועד inside the case of the ox. The answer is that the משנה deals only with a מועד, so a תם was never on the table. That means the משנה gives no proof either way about חצי נזק.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox with a record of goring, whose owner pays full damages
It is talking about, it deals with

phrases.english: The entire [משנה] is talking about a מועד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5 and keeps the rejection of step 3 standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the whole משנה deals only with a מועד.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the משנה did not single out a תם, a תם must also pay on admission.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה never addresses a תם, so its silence proves nothing about חצי נזק.

steps.title: New proof from 'paying more than the damage'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the closing rule of the משנה. Whoever pays more than the damage does not pay on his own admission. This implies that whoever pays less, like a תם paying חצי נזק, does pay on admission. That would make חצי נזק ממון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: This is the rule: anyone who pays more than what he damaged does not pay based on his own admission. Doesn't that mean that someone who pays less than what he damaged does pay?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new proof that חצי נזק is ממון. It uses the general rule at the end of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying more than the damage is a penalty, so admitting to it does not obligate you. The גמרא reads the rule closely: only 'more' was excluded. So 'less' (חצי נזק of a תם) must be payable on admission, and that is a sign of ממון.

keyTerms.meaning: More than the amount of the damage (a penalty payment)
Is it not that...? Introduces an inference

steps.confusionAlert: 'Paying less than the damage' is not about a cheap payment. It points to the תם ox, whose owner pays only half the damage.

phrases.english: Come and hear: This is the rule:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמְשַׁלֵּם יוֹתֵר עַל מַה שֶּׁהִזִּיק –
phrases.english: anyone who pays more than what he damaged
does not pay based on his own admission.
What, is it not
that one who pays less than what he damaged does pay?
phrases.notes: 'Less than the damage' means the תם ox's half payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was turned away, a new proof is brought from the end of the same משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The closing rule of the משנה, read by inference: only 'more than the damage' is excluded from paying on admission.

steps.title: Maybe only the exact amount pays on admission
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inference. The rule may mean that only someone paying exactly the damage pays on admission. Then both 'more' and 'less' would not.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means that one who pays exactly as much as he damaged does pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It offers a different way to read what the rule implies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opposite of 'more than the damage' does not have to be 'less'. It could be 'exactly the damage'. If so, a תם paying half might also not pay on admission, and the proof is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Exactly as much as he damaged

phrases.english: No, [it implies only that] one who pays as much as he damaged does pay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the inference 'less pays'. The rule itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Step 7 assumed the opposite of 'more' is 'less'. It could just as well be 'exactly the same amount'.

steps.title: So would 'less' not pay either?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא checks what the rejection means. If only the exact amount pays, then someone paying less also does not pay on admission.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about 'less'? Would you say he indeed does not pay?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out what the rejection must mean for someone paying less. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the rejection's reading, someone paying less, like the owner of a תם, would not pay on his own admission. The גמרא states this clearly so it can test it against the wording of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Indeed so: is that really the case?

phrases.english: But [one who pays] less, what [is the law]?
Would you say he indeed does not pay?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל פָּחוֹת מַאי הָכִי נָמֵי דְּלָא מְשַׁלֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what the rejection in step 8 means for someone paying less than the damage.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the rejection's reading mean that someone paying less than the damage also does not pay on admission?

steps.title: Then the משנה should have used broader wording
steps.stepSummary: If both 'more' and 'less' do not pay on admission, the משנה should have said 'anyone who does not pay exactly the damage.' That would cover both. Since it said only 'more,' 'less' must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, instead of teaching 'This is the rule: anyone who pays more than what he damaged does not pay on his own admission,' let it teach 'This is the rule: anyone who does not pay as much as he damaged.' That wording would mean both less and more!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection from the wording of the משנה. If 'less' also did not pay, the משנה would have chosen wording that covers both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'does not pay as much as he damaged' would include paying more and paying less in one short rule. The משנה picked the narrower phrase 'more than the damage'. That shows only 'more' is excluded, so 'less', the תם's חצי נזק, does pay on admission.

phrases.english: If so, instead of teaching:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כׇּל הַמְשַׁלֵּם יוֹתֵר עַל מַה שֶּׁהִזִּיק –
phrases.english: This is the rule: anyone who pays more than what he damaged
does not pay based on his own admission;
let it teach: This is the rule:
anyone who does not pay as much as he damaged
which means less, and also means more!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading proposed in steps 8–9 by checking it against the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rejection's claim that only the exact amount pays on admission, so 'less' does not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both more and less were excluded, the משנה would have said 'anyone who does not pay as much as he damaged'. Choosing 'more' shows that only 'more' is excluded.

steps.title: Refuted: חצי נזק is not a penalty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares a תיובתא, a final refutation of the view that חצי נזק is a קנס.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion: the rejection failed, so the proof from step 7 stands. The view that חצי נזק is a קנס is refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'less than the damage' does pay on one's own admission, the תם's חצי נזק works like ממון. A קנס is not paid on admission, so the view that calls חצי נזק a קנס cannot stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Half damages, paid by the owner of a תם ox
A penalty, which is not paid based on one's own admission

steps.whatToRemember: At this point the גמרא reads the closing rule of the משנה as excluding only someone paying MORE than the damage. So a תם's חצי נזק (LESS than the damage) would be paid on admission, which refutes the view that חצי נזק is a קנס. Steps 14-15 show this refutation is not airtight, and the הלכה goes the other way.
steps.whyThisMatters: Whether חצי נזק is ממון or קנס decides things like whether one pays it based on one's own admission. This is a basic question for the whole topic of a תם ox.

phrases.english: This is a refutation.
phrases.notes: It refutes the view that the תם's half payment is a penalty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of step 10 by declaring the opposing view refuted.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's wording shows that whoever pays less than the damage pays on his own admission. So the view that חצי נזק is a קנס is refuted.

steps.title: The ruling: half damages is a fine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה is פלגא נזקא קנסא, even though it just refuted that view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: half damages is a fine.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after the תיובתא, the גמרא states the final הלכה: the half payment of a שור תם is a קנס. This sets up a surprised question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the exact view that step 11 just knocked down. Stating it as הלכה looks like a contradiction. The גמרא will now explain why the refutation was not truly final.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law, the final ruling
Half damages, what a תם pays
A fine, a penalty rather than plain repayment of a loss

steps.whyThisMatters: In practice, half damages is treated as a קנס. One result: a person does not pay it based on his own admission.

phrases.english: And the halakha is:
half damages is a fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical ruling that seems to clash with the תיובתא in step 11

steps.title: How can a refuted view be the law?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a view can be both refuted and the הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A refutation, and also the הלכה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out the clash: we just said תיובתא, and now we rule like the refuted view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a תיובתא means the view is rejected. A rejected view cannot be the practical law. So either the refutation or the ruling must give way.

keyTerms.meaning: A final refutation, the view is knocked down

phrases.english: A conclusive refutation and the halakha?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 12 using the תיובתא of step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that פלגא נזקא קנסא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A view that received a תיובתא cannot also be the הלכה

steps.title: Pinpointing what the refutation rested on
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says yes, it can be the law, and recalls that the refutation rested only on the משנה not saying 'exactly as he damaged.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. What was the reason it was a refutation? Because the משנה does not say 'as much as he damaged.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer. It says 'yes, it can be the law' and points to the weak spot in the refutation. This sets up the real answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole תיובתא came from one wording point. The משנה said 'more than the damage' instead of 'not exactly the damage,' which seemed to show that 'less' does pay on admission. If that wording can be explained another way, the refutation falls.

keyTerms.meaning: Exactly as much as he damaged

phrases.english: Yes.
What is the reason it was a refutation?
Because it does not teach 'as much as he damaged.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering step 13 by naming the basis of the תיובתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Undermining the basis of the refutation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's wording proves that 'less' pays on admission
steps.terutzMaskana: The wording proof depends on the משנה having been able to write 'exactly,' which the next step will deny

steps.title: The pebbles case blocks a sweeping rule
steps.stepSummary: The משנה could not say 'anyone who does not pay exactly' because חצי נזק צרורות is paying less, and it is ממון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה cannot make a sweeping statement. There is half damages for pebbles, which we know by tradition is ממון. That is why it does not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real answer. The משנה could not write 'whoever does not pay exactly the damage does not pay on admission,' because one case of paying less, צרורות, is ממון and does pay on admission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'less' is not one uniform group, the משנה could not lump it in. So its silence about 'less' says nothing about a תם's half damages. The תיובתא falls away, and the ruling that פלגא נזקא קנסא stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He cannot make it a sweeping, no-exceptions rule
Half damages for pebbles kicked up by an animal while walking
Learned as a הלכה by tradition
Plain repayment of a loss, not a fine

steps.whatToRemember: The תיובתא was only a wording proof. Because חצי נזק צרורות is ממון, the משנה could not write a blanket rule for everyone who pays less. So a תם's half damages can still be a קנס, and that is the הלכה.
steps.confusionAlert: There are two different 'half damages.' A תם's goring half damages is a קנס. Pebbles half damages is ממון, known by tradition. Do not mix them up.

phrases.english: He cannot state it absolutely.
Since there is half damages for pebbles,
phrases.notes: These are pebbles an animal kicks up while walking normally, and they cause damage.

phrases.english: which we learned by tradition is monetary restitution;
because of this, it does not teach it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer begun in step 14 and removes the basis of the תיובתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the משנה's wording another way
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה left out 'less' because 'less' pays on admission, so חצי נזק is ממון
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה left out 'less' because 'less' includes צרורות, which is ממון. A תם's half damages can still be a קנס
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The refutation is undone, and the הלכה is פלגא נזקא קנסא

steps.title: Unusual attacks by dogs and cats are not collected in Babylonia
steps.stepSummary: Because חצי נזק is a קנס, a dog eating lambs or a cat eating a chicken counts as unusual, and the payment is not collected in בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And now that you have said that half-damage is a fine: a dog that ate lambs, or a cat that ate a chicken, is acting unusually, and we do not collect this payment in Babylonia.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the ruling it just made, that פלגא נזקא קנסא, and shows a real-life result of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dog eating lambs or a cat eating a chicken is not normal for these animals. So it counts as unusual damage, and for an animal that has never done this before, the owner pays only חצי נזק. Since that half payment is a קנס, the courts in בבל do not collect it, because they do not collect fines.

keyTerms.meaning: A fine, a penalty that is not simple repayment of money

steps.whyThisMatters: This is where the theoretical question 'is חצי נזק ממון or קנס?' becomes a practical question of whether a court in בבל will collect at all.

phrases.english: And now that you have said
half-damage is a fine
this dog that ate lambs
and a cat that ate a chicken
it is unusual
and we do not collect it in Babylonia

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical result from the ruling that פלגא נזקא קנסא, now that steps 13-15 have explained how the ruling stands despite the תיובתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dog eating lambs or a cat eating a chicken is unusual damage. Its חצי נזק is a קנס and is not collected in בבל.

steps.title: Small animals are normal food, so the payment is collected
steps.stepSummary: The rule of step 16 applies only to large lambs and chickens. Eating small ones is normal behavior.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only to large ones. But with small ones, that is the animal's normal way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the rule it just gave. It applies only when the dog or cat attacked large animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a dog or cat, eating a small lamb or chicken is normal behavior, not an unusual attack. Normal eating is full payment, which is plain ממון, so courts in בבל can collect it. Only attacks on large animals count as מְשׁוּנֶּה and fall under the קנס rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Its normal way, its usual behavior

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think every case of a dog eating a lamb is uncollectible in בבל. With small animals it is normal eating, full payment, and it is collected.

phrases.english: And this applies only to large ones
phrases.notes: He means large lambs and large chickens.

phrases.english: but with small ones
it is its normal way

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits step 16's rule to large animals only.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only attacks on large animals are מְשׁוּנֶּה. Eating small animals is normal behavior and is paid in full.

steps.title: If the victim seized payment, we do not take it back
steps.stepSummary: Even when the payment is a קנס that בבל courts cannot collect, a victim who grabbed the owner's property keeps it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he seized, we do not take it away from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that the victim is not left helpless. If he grabbed payment himself, the court lets him keep it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not collecting a קנס in בבל does not mean the money is not owed. It only means the court there cannot make the owner pay. So if the victim already took payment on his own, the court will not take it back from him.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not take out (from his hands)

phrases.english: And if he seized
phrases.notes: The victim grabbed something belonging to the animal's owner to cover his loss.

phrases.english: we do not take it away from him

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a remedy for the victim in the uncollectible קנס case of step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A victim who seizes payment for a קנס keeps it. בבל courts do not force him to return it.

steps.title: Setting a time to go to court in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: If the victim asks for a set time to take the case to ארץ ישראל, the court sets it. If the owner does not go, he is placed in נידוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he says, 'Set a time for me, because I will go to the land of Israel,' we set it for him. And if the other one does not go, we place him in נידוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the victim one more option: the court in בבל can send the case to ארץ ישראל and enforce the summons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The courts of ארץ ישראל can collect a קנס, even though the courts of בבל cannot. So the בבל court sets a date for both sides to appear there. If the animal's owner refuses to go, the בבל court puts him in נידוי for ignoring its order.

keyTerms.meaning: We place him under נידוי (a ban)

steps.whatToRemember: Since פלגא נזקא קנסא, an unusual attack's חצי נזק is not collected in בבל. Still, the victim has three protections: eating small animals is normal and is paid in full, whatever he seizes he keeps, and he can force the case to ארץ ישראל on pain of נידוי.

phrases.english: And if he says
Set a time for me
because I will go to the land of Israel
we set it for him
And if he does not go
phrases.notes: The 'he' here switches to the animal's owner, the one being summoned.

phrases.english: we place him under a ban

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמַר: קִבְעוּ לִי זִימְנָא, דְּאָזֵילְנָא לְאַרְעָא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second remedy beyond seizing: the court in בבל arranges a hearing in ארץ ישראל and enforces it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court sets a time for a hearing in ארץ ישראל when the victim asks for one. An owner who refuses to go is placed under נידוי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The קנס status of חצי נזק limits collection in בבל but does not cancel the debt.

steps.title: The owner is placed in נידוי until he removes the danger
steps.stepSummary: Whatever happens with the case, the court places the owner in נידוי until he gets rid of the dangerous animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Either way, we place him in נידוי until he removes the thing that causes damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more rule to the case from step 19. No matter how the case turns out, the owner stays in נידוי until he gets rid of the danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 used נידוי to push the owner to go to court in ארץ ישראל. This step adds a separate reason for נידוי: he is keeping something dangerous. That second reason lasts until the danger is gone, whatever happens with the money.

keyTerms.meaning: We place him in שמתא (a form of נידוי, being cut off from the community)
The thing that causes damage, here the dangerous animal
Either way, no matter which way it goes

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the court can still act even when it cannot collect a קנס. Its goal here is to protect people from future harm.

phrases.english: And either way,
we place him in נידוי
until he removes the danger

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ, מְשַׁמְּתִינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further rule to the נידוי case of step 19
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner of a dangerous animal is kept in נידוי until he removes the danger.

steps.title: The source for removing dangers: רבי נתן and the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The rule comes from רבי נתן, who learns from 'לא תשים דמים בביתך' that one may not keep a vicious dog or a shaky ladder at home.
steps.simpleTranslation: This comes from רבי נתן. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי נתן says, from where do we learn that a person may not raise a vicious dog in his house, and may not set up a shaky ladder in his house? The פסוק says: 'You shall not put blood in your house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the rule in step 20. רבי נתן learns from a פסוק that a person may not keep dangerous things in his house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about putting a railing on a roof, but רבי נתן reads it as a general ban on keeping any danger at home. Since keeping a dangerous animal breaks this איסור, the court may place the owner in נידוי until he fixes it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Do not put blood in your house', meaning do not leave a deadly danger in your home

steps.whatToRemember: A person may not keep a danger on his property. Based on רבי נתן's reading of 'לא תשים דמים בביתך', the court places the owner in נידוי until the danger is removed.

phrases.english: From the ruling of רבי נתן.
As it is taught: רבי נתן says:
From where do we learn that a person may not raise
a vicious dog in his house,
and may not set up a shaky ladder
in his house?
The פסוק says:
"You shall not put blood in your house."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּרַבִּי נָתָן. דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source that justifies the נידוי in step 20
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the owner is kept in נידוי until he removes the danger
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי נתן reading דברים 22:8 as a ban on keeping any danger at home

steps.title: New משנה: five acts of a תם and five of a מועד
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens by saying there are five acts for which an animal is a תם and five for which it is a מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: There are five that are תם and five that are מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a heading that sets up two lists. Next it will spell out the five acts for which an animal is a תם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that is a תם pays only חצי נזק. An animal that is a מועד pays full damages. This heading tells us the משנה will sort damaging acts into these two groups of five.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals that are תם: not yet known for this kind of damage, so the owner pays half
Animals that are מועד: known for this damage, so the owner pays in full

steps.confusionAlert: The 'five and five' are kinds of damaging acts, not five animals. Each act is listed with the rule that applies to it.

phrases.english: משנה:
Five are תם
and five are מועד

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Damaging acts are sorted into five that are תם and five that are מועד.

steps.title: The five acts for which an animal starts out as a תם
steps.stepSummary: An animal is not considered מועד for goring, pushing, biting, crouching, or kicking.
steps.simpleTranslation: An animal is not considered מועד for goring, for pushing, for biting, for crouching, or for kicking.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists the first group from its heading: the five acts for which an animal starts out as a תם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These five acts are unusual for an ordinary animal. That is why the animal starts out as a תם for them, and the owner pays only חצי נזק unless the animal has become a מועד.

keyTerms.meaning: To crouch or lie down on something and damage it

steps.whatToRemember: For goring, pushing, biting, crouching, and kicking, an animal starts out as a תם and the owner pays חצי נזק.

phrases.english: An animal is not considered מועד
not for goring, nor for pushing,
nor for biting, nor for crouching,
phrases.notes: 'Crouching' here means lying down on something in a way that damages it.

phrases.english: nor for kicking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first list announced in step 22
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Goring, pushing, biting, crouching, and kicking are acts for which an animal starts out as a תם.

steps.title: The five cases where the owner pays in full
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the five מועד cases: tooth, foot, a forewarned ox, an ox damaging in the victim's property, and a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: The tooth is forewarned to eat what is fit for it. The foot is forewarned to break things as it walks. Also the forewarned ox, an ox that damages in the victim's property, and a person.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the second list it promised: the five cases that count as מועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 listed five acts that are not מועד. Here are the five that are, meaning the owner pays full damages. שן and רגל are normal animal behavior, so they are מועד from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: Tooth: damage done by an animal eating
Foot: damage done by an animal walking normally
The property of the person who was harmed

phrases.aramaic: הַשֵּׁן – מוּעֶדֶת לֶאֱכוֹל אֶת הָרָאוּי לָהּ;
phrases.english: The tooth is forewarned to eat what is fit for it;
the foot is forewarned to break things as it walks;
and the forewarned ox;
and an ox that damages in the property of the injured party;
and the person.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשֵּׁן – מוּעֶדֶת לֶאֱכוֹל אֶת הָרָאוּי לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of the opening list from step 22, after step 23's list of תם acts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שן, רגל, שור המועד, an ox damaging in the victim's property, and אדם are all מועד.

steps.title: Wild animals are forewarned from the start
steps.stepSummary: Wolf, lion, bear, leopard, ברדלס and snake are מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wolf, the lion, the bear, the leopard, the ברדלס and the snake are all forewarned.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a rule for wild animals: they count as מועד right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A domestic ox starts as a תם and only becomes מועד after repeated goring. Wild animals are dangerous by nature, so they are treated as מועד even before they have caused any damage.

phrases.english: The wolf, the lion, and the bear,
and the leopard, the bardelas, and the snake,
these are forewarned.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַזְּאֵב וְהָאֲרִי וְהַדּוֹב וְהַנָּמֵר וְהַבַּרְדְּלָס וְהַנָּחָשׁ – הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מוּעָדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the מועד list from domestic animals to wild animals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wild animals are מועד even without a history of damage.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: tame wild animals are not forewarned, except the snake
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says tamed wild animals are not מועד, but a snake is always מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: when they are tamed, they are not forewarned. But the snake is always forewarned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר disagrees in part and limits the previous rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעזר, a wild animal that has been domesticated loses its automatic מועד status. He makes one exception: a snake stays dangerous no matter what, so it is always מועד.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's full list: five kinds of מועד, plus wild animals. רבי אלעזר exempts tame ones but never the snake.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
when they are domesticated,
they are not forewarned.
And the snake is always forewarned.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵן בְּנֵי תַרְבּוּת – אֵינָן מוּעָדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a dissenting view that limits step 25's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tame wild animals are not מועד, but a snake always is.

steps.title: The גמרא infers the משנה is set in the victim's courtyard
steps.stepSummary: Since שן is listed as מועד, the משנה must be about the victim's courtyard, and there a תם that gores still pays half.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the משנה teaches that the tooth is forewarned to eat, we see that we are dealing with the injured party's courtyard. And it teaches that an animal is not forewarned to pay in full, but it does pay half damages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by reading the משנה closely and drawing two facts from it. This sets up the next step's question of who wrote the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Listing שן as liable shows the case happens in the victim's courtyard, where eating damage is paid for. Then the first list says goring there is 'not מועד,' meaning no full payment, so a half payment is still owed. Together these show that a תם goring in the victim's courtyard pays half.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
The courtyard of the person harmed
Half the cost of the damage

phrases.english: GEMARA
From the fact that it teaches 'the tooth is forewarned to eat,'
we learn that we are dealing with the courtyard of the injured party;
and it teaches that an animal is not forewarned,
meaning, to pay all of it;
but it does pay half damages.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָתָנֵי הַשֵּׁן מוּעֶדֶת לֶאֱכוֹל – מִכְּלָל דְּבַחֲצַר הַנִּיזָּק עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by reading the two lists of the משנה together.

steps.title: The משנה follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: Who holds this? The רבנן, who say an unusual goring in the victim's courtyard pays half.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is the רבנן, who say that goring, which is unusual behavior, in the injured party's courtyard pays half damages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies whose opinion the משנה follows, based on the inference it just made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that a תם goring in the victim's courtyard pays only half is the view of the רבנן. So the anonymous משנה must follow them. Goring is called משונה because it is not normal animal behavior.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is it? Whose view is this?

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה is set in the victim's courtyard and follows the רבנן: a תם goring there pays חצי נזק.

phrases.english: Who is it? It is the Rabbis,
who say: an unusual goring in the courtyard of the injured party,
it is half damages that he pays.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers whose view fits the inference drawn in step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a תם goring in the victim's courtyard pays half?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן, who rule that משונה קרן in חצר הניזק pays חצי נזק.

steps.title: The end of the list sounds like רבי טרפון
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא lists 'an ox damaging in the victim's property' as מועד, paying full. That fits רבי טרפון, not the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now read the end of the list: a forewarned ox, an ox that damages in the victim's property, and a person. This brings us to רבי טרפון, who says an unusual goring in the victim's courtyard pays full damages!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the second half of the משנה's list and points out that it seems to follow a different opinion than the first half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 28 we said the רישא follows the רבנן: a תם goring in the victim's courtyard pays only half. But the סיפא treats 'an ox damaging in the victim's property' as a separate מועד case that pays full. Only רבי טרפון says a goring there pays full, so the סיפא seems to follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter part of a משנה or ברייתא
We have arrived at (the opinion of)
Unusual. Goring is not the animal's normal behavior

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same משנה as step 27. The רישא (with שן) was shown to follow the רבנן. Now the סיפא of that same list seems to follow רבי טרפון. The problem is the switch, not either half on its own.

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
a forewarned ox,
and an ox that damages in the property of the injured party,
and the person.
We have arrived at רבי טרפון, who says:
an unusual act, goring, in the courtyard of the injured party,
it is full damages that he pays!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the conclusion of step 28 (the רישא follows the רבנן) against the סיפא of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the whole משנה follows the רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא calls a goring in the victim's property מועד and makes it pay full, which is רבי טרפון's view, not the רבנן's.

steps.title: Can one משנה switch opinions midway?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in surprise: could the רישא follow the רבנן and the סיפא follow רבי טרפון?
steps.simpleTranslation: The start follows the רבנן and the end follows רבי טרפון?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up the strange result of the last two steps and asks in surprise whether that can really be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we expect a single משנה to follow one consistent opinion. Splitting it between two opposing views looks unlikely, so this question challenges the reading.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a משנה

phrases.english: The first clause is the רבנן,
and the latter clause is רבי טרפון?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the surprising result of step 29 combined with step 28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is it acceptable for one משנה to follow two different opinions?
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the משנה as following the רבנן (step 28) while its סיפא follows רבי טרפון (step 29)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single משנה is expected to follow one consistent opinion. Splitting it between two opposing views seems unacceptable.

steps.title: Yes, as שמואל told רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Yes. שמואל told רב יהודה to follow his reading, in which the רישא is the רבנן and the סיפא is רבי טרפון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. שמואל said to רב יהודה: 'Sharp-toothed one, leave the משנה and follow me: the רישא is the רבנן and the סיפא is רבי טרפון.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the split really is correct, and backs it up with a statement from שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל himself explained this משנה as split between two opinions. So the surprising reading from steps 29-30 is accepted, not rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Sharp-toothed one,' a nickname שמואל used for רב יהודה
Come after me, follow my reading

steps.whatToRemember: According to this approach, the list of five מועדין is split. The part with שן follows the רבנן (a goring in the victim's courtyard pays half). The part with 'an ox damaging in the victim's property' follows רבי טרפון (full payment).

phrases.english: Yes,
for שמואל said to רב יהודה:
Sharp-toothed one,
phrases.notes: This is a nickname שמואל used for his student רב יהודה.

phrases.english: leave the משנה and come follow me:
the first clause is the רבנן and the latter clause is רבי טרפון.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, דְּהָאָמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the surprised question of step 30 by accepting the split.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the difficulty as correct, supported by an אמורא's statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A single משנה should follow one opinion throughout.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל explicitly reads this משנה as רישא following the רבנן and סיפא following רבי טרפון.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר quoting רב opens a new explanation
steps.stepSummary: An introduction: רבי אלעזר, in the name of רב, is about to give a different reading of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רב:
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. The גמרא is about to bring a different way to explain the משנה, from רבי אלעזר quoting רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only says who is speaking. His actual words come right after it. It opens a new approach, apparently one that will avoid splitting the משנה between two opinions.

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רב:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second approach to the משנה after the split-opinion approach of step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An attribution only. The content of רב's explanation follows in the next lines.
